{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that cleanliness priming would lead to less severe moral judgments than neutral priming among participants exerting low response effort, but that this effect would be absent or reversed among participants exerting high response effort.",
  "design": "mixed, with priming condition (cleanliness vs. neutral) as a between-subjects factor and response effort (low vs. high) as a between-subjects manipulation.",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Participants were randomly assigned to either a low response effort condition (instructed to work as quickly as possible and not worry about accuracy) or a high response effort condition (instructed to work quickly but perform to the best of their ability) during a sentence unscrambling task containing either cleanliness-related or neutral words.",
  "outcome_measure": "A composite score of moral judgments across six vignettes (dog, trolley, wallet, plane, résumé, kitten) rated on a 10-point scale from 0 (perfectly ok) to 9 (extremely wrong).",
  "population_and_setting": "English-speaking adults residing in the United States recruited via Amazon Mechanical Turk.",
  "sample_size_total": 440,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Recruited from Amazon Mechanical Turk in exchange for $0.50 compensation.",
  "analysis_plan": "A 2 (priming condition) x 2 (response effort condition) factorial ANOVA to test for an interaction effect, followed by simple effects tests.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "Participants were excluded if they guessed the study hypothesis or if they responded faster than 675 words per minute on two or more moral vignettes (rapid insufficient effort responding)."
}
